title: Detectors
description: Reference for every detector Latet ships.

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_reference.py from the code: do not edit by hand. -->

Every request passes through these detectors, in this order of priority when two find the same
text: secrets first, then your terms and this machine's identity, then personal data. A detector
marked *fail-closed* stops the request if it fails, rather than letting text through unchecked.

| Detector | Finds | Kind | Profiles | If it fails |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `latet-credentials` | Latet personal tokens, computer keys, API keys and administration tokens, and route keys in HTTPS identity addresses. | secret | all | fail-closed |
| `gitleaks` | API keys and tokens of known services, with the gitleaks ruleset: patterns, keywords, entropy thresholds and allowlists as gitleaks applies them. | secret | all | fail-closed |
| `assignment` | Values assigned to sensitive names (``DB_PASSWORD=…``, ``"api_key": "…"``, ``$env:TOKEN = …``). | secret | all | fail-closed |
| `private-key` | The whole body of a PEM/OpenSSH/PGP private key block (header and footer stay visible). | secret | all | fail-closed |
| `credentials` | Passwords in ``scheme://user:pass@host``, JWTs and bearer/basic credentials. | secret | all | fail-closed |
| `fields` | Values by the field they sit in: secret names, your field rules and strict data mode. | secret; your fields; data values | all | fail-closed |
| `pii` | Structured personal data, each match validated (checksums, number plans, the IANA TLD list). | personal data | `balanced`, `max` | skipped, request flagged |
| `terms` | The user's deny-list (client names, project code names, internal domains...). | your terms | all (when you add terms) | fail-closed |
| `identity` | This machine's identity: the OS user inside home paths, the host name, the git author and its company's domain. | identity | `balanced`, `max` | fail-closed |
| `known-values` | Every original already in the vault, matched exactly wherever it appears again. | any | all | fail-closed |

## Latet credentials

These built-in secret types apply in every profile, on a computer and in a server space.
They use the same policies, allow lists, conversation restoration and outbound-tool checks as other secrets.

| Type | Recognised value | Fake |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `LATET_PERSONAL_TOKEN` | `latet_pat_` followed by 43 URL-safe characters. | Public prefix and length kept; secret tail drawn again. |
| `LATET_COMPUTER_KEY` | `latet_ck_` followed by 43 URL-safe characters. | Public prefix and length kept; secret tail drawn again. |
| `LATET_API_KEY` | `latet_key_` followed by 43 URL-safe characters. | Public prefix and length kept; secret tail drawn again. |
| `LATET_ADMIN_TOKEN` | `latet_adm_` followed by 43 URL-safe characters. | Public prefix and length kept; secret tail drawn again. |
| `LATET_ROUTE_KEY` | The 16 to 128 URL-safe characters after `/u/` in `https://<host>/u/<route-key>`. | Entire route key drawn again; host and other path segments kept. |

URL-safe characters are `A-Z`, `a-z`, `0-9`, `_` and `-`. A credential is matched as a complete token;
a route key as a complete path segment. Only the route key is replaced in an identity address.

## Personal data

| Type | How a match is confirmed |
| --- | --- |
| `EMAIL` | Top-level domain checked against the IANA list (shipped offline). |
| `PHONE` | Parsed and validated with libphonenumber; numbers without a prefix only for `phone_regions`. Decimals, dates, versions and digit lists are skipped. |
| `IBAN` | Country length and ISO 13616 mod-97 checksum. |
| `CREDIT_CARD` | Issuer prefix (IIN) and Luhn checksum; repeated digits are skipped. |
| `IP_ADDRESS` | Public IPv4 and IPv6 addresses (private ones too with `include_private_ips`); version-like numbers are skipped. |
| `CRYPTO_WALLET` | Bitcoin addresses with a valid Base58Check or bech32/bech32m checksum. |
| `VAT_NUMBER` | With the country prefix (EL for Greece, CHE for Switzerland), checked by each country's check digits; an Italian partita IVA is `IT_VAT_CODE` while that type is on. |

## National ID and tax numbers

Recognised for the countries in `id_regions` (the `max` profile: every country). A keyword is
a word such as *SSN* or *Steuer-ID* on the same line, a few characters away, or in the column
header of a table. Numbers are never taken from inside longer numbers, versions, decimals or paths.

| Country | Type | Number | Written | How a match is confirmed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| BE | `BE_NATIONAL_NUMBER` | National register number (rijksregisternummer) | `NN.NN.NN-NNN.NN` | Birth date and mod-97 check digits. Written without separators, only next to a keyword. |
| CA | `CA_SIN` | Social Insurance Number (SIN) | `NNN NNN NNN` | Luhn check digit; always next to a keyword (`SIN` in capitals only, never `sin(`). |
| CH | `CH_AHV` | AHV/AVS number (social security) | `756.NNNN.NNNN.NN` | Starts with 756; EAN-13 check digit. |
| DE | `DE_TAX_ID` | Tax ID (Steuer-IdNr) | `NN NNN NNN NNN` | Digit repetition rule and ISO 7064 MOD 11,10; always next to a keyword. |
| ES | `ES_DNI` | DNI (Documento Nacional de Identidad) | `NNNNNNNNA` | Check letter: the number modulo 23. |
| ES | `ES_NIE` | NIE (Número de Identidad de Extranjero) | `ANNNNNNNA` | X, Y or Z, seven digits and a check letter (modulo 23). |
| FI | `FI_HETU` | Personal identity code (henkilötunnus) | `NNNNNN-NNNA` | Birth date, century sign and check character (modulo 31). |
| FR | `FR_NIR` | Social security number (NIR) | `N NN NN NN NNN NNN NN` | Sex, birth year and month, place; mod-97 key. Written without spaces, only next to a keyword. |
| GB | `GB_NINO` | National Insurance number | `AA NN NN NN A` | Issued prefixes and suffix. In code, only next to a keyword. |
| IT | `IT_FISCAL_CODE` | Codice fiscale | `AAAAAANNANNANNNA` | Structure (letters, birth date, place) and check character. |
| IT | `IT_VAT_CODE` | Partita IVA | `NNNNNNNNNNN` | Check digit, with an `IT` prefix or a VAT word on the same line. |
| LV | `LV_PERSONAL_CODE` | Personal code (personas kods) | `NNNNNN-NNNNN` | Birth date (a code issued since July 2017 starts with 32 instead) and check digit. Written without the hyphen, only next to a keyword. |
| NL | `NL_BSN` | Citizen service number (BSN) | `NNNN.NN.NNN` | The 11 test; always next to a keyword. |
| PL | `PL_PESEL` | PESEL | `NNNNNNNNNNN` | Birth date and weighted check digit. In code, only next to a keyword. |
| PT | `PT_NIF` | Tax number (NIF, número de contribuinte) | `NNN NNN NNN` | Weighted mod-11 check digit; always next to a keyword. |
| SE | `SE_PERSONNUMMER` | Personnummer | `NNNNNN-NNNN` | Birth date and Luhn check digit. In code, only next to a keyword. |
| US | `US_SSN` | Social Security number | `NNN-NN-NNNN` | Issued area, group and serial ranges; always next to a keyword. |
| US | `US_ITIN` | Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN) | `9NN-NN-NNNN` | Starts with 9, issued group ranges; always next to a keyword. |

## Fields of tool outputs

The `fields` detector reads the structures of a text: psql, CSV, TSV, markdown and HTML tables,
the tables of a browser's accessibility snapshot, lines of `key=value` pairs, `"key": value`
fragments, and JSON documents value by value, each with its path (`items[].sku`). Values of one
or two characters stay in clear. A value found by its field is masked in its structure only: the
same word elsewhere is left alone. See [Production data](../../concepts/production-data/).

| Rule | Masks |
| --- | --- |
| `field-secret:<field>` | The value of a column or key named like a secret (`password_hash`, `api_key`, `reset_token`), always. |
| `field:<name>` | The values of a field one of your [field rules](../configuration/#fields-items) names. |
| `strict:<field>` | In strict data mode (`data: strict`), any other value of a tool's output. |

Strict data mode leaves alone the output of the tools that read files: `glob`, `grep`, `list_dir`, `list_directory`, `ls`, `notebookread`, `read`, `read_file`, `search_files`, `view`, unless `data_files` names the file one of them returns (`notebookread`, `read`, `read_file`, `view`); and that of the web tools, unless `data_tools` names them or `data_hosts` the address: `web_fetch`, `web_search`, `webfetch`, `websearch`. The lines a tool shows of a file it changed are read as the file when `data_files` names it, whatever `data_tools` names: `edit`, `edit_file`, `multiedit`, `notebookedit`, `write`, `write_file`.
